rendered: The anode-free full cell, built with a presodiated pyrite cathode, reaches an energy density of ∼400 Wh/kg[1]. The paper says this is calculated on the mass of the presodiated pyrite and the carbon nucleation layer. This is said to exceed all previous reports for sodium-ion batteries. The stated theoretical maximum for LIB technology is 387 Wh/kg for LiCoO2/graphite cells[2]. So the anode-free sodium cell's value sits slightly above that LiCoO2/graphite ceiling on this basis. The authors add that, assuming a 50%[3] packaging penalty, it exceeds current LIB technology[4]. Taken together, the comparison is favourable but close, and it rests on the cell-level assumptions described above.
